newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia presents final draft privatisation law.
newsitem.headline: Serbia presents final draft privatisation law.

text.p: Serbia, criticised for slow progress on economic reform, presented on Thursday a final version of its draft privatisation law.
The law will be submitted to parliament at the end of June for adoption.
"This is the best and the most modern law ever made in a transition economy," Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic told Reuters.
The law, substantially changed from its first draft, falls short of mass voucher privatisation used in other former communist countries.
It envisages heavy discounts, allows companies to decide themselves whether to privatise, relies heavily on privatisation to employees and includes between four and five million people.
According to some estimates, around 100 billion German marks ($58 billion) worth of socially-owned and state-owned assets will be subject to privatisation.

"The law does not incorporate any force (to privatise) but at the same time prevents... any wild privatisation, envisaging a procedure for the transformation process," Marjanovic told a meeting of businessmen and bankers.
Marjanovic insisted reforms would be absolutely transparent and privatisation would be socially fair and in line with the constitution.
Economists have criticised Serbia for a slow pace of reform compared with other post-communist states.

But Marjanovic said 1997 had rightfully been declared the year of reforms. Their implementation was a key precondition for restructuring the Serbian economy and its integration with the world economy.
"I am sure that an investment climate will improve after the adoption of this law because foreign investors and partners will know exactly who owes what and what they buy," he said.
Marjanovic was confident privatisation would attract external capital and said he expected foreign capital inflow to boost Serbia's growth rate.
The law has been sent to the parliament and will be on the agenda at its June 30 session.
-- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254 ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
